text:
kevin: heads up — BLEU numbers for the int8 build just tanked on nightly eval compared to float32. not sure if it's a metric bug or tokenization mismatch.

marta: hmm, tanked how much?

kevin: corpus BLEU dropped from 27.8 -> 12.3 for wmt-ish testset. exact same hypotheses on disk when i diffed them, so model outputs look fine.

jon: that smells like a scoring change. did sacrebleu version or smoothing params change in the runner?

kevin: runner pinned sacrebleu 2.3 before, CI image upgraded to 2.5 in last deploy (see build 8792). look at this log excerpt from eval-bot: 

eval-bot: run_id=run-2026-03-15-8792 status=completed metrics={"bleu":12.3, "rougeL":45.1}

tara: also check corpus vs sentence-level averaging. our harness accidentally switched to averaging sentence BLEU then mean, instead of corpus BLEU. that could cause huge diffs.

ali: past threads — we had a bug where weight normalization used integer division when token counts were int32. check metric implementation in runner/metrics/bleu.py.

kevin: digging — open file shows: 

```
# runner/metrics/bleu.py
weights = counts // total_counts  # oops
score = bleu_from_counts(weights)
```

kevin: yep that's integer division. but weirdly that file hasn't changed in months. commit range shows an unrelated refactor touched imports and upgraded sacrebleu in same PR: 9a3f2b4. maybe combination exposed the issue.

marta: good catch. integer division would zero-out fractional weights leading to tiny BLEU. that explains the drop.

jon: patch suggestion: cast to float and ensure weights sum==1.0, plus add unit tests for a tiny toy case.

ali: also add a guard for tokenization differences — runner should pass the same tokenizer config we used during decoding. we had earlier mismatches between sacrebleu.tokenize=13 (intl) vs our tokenizer. add explicit tok arg.

kevin: i'm putting up a quick PR to fix division and pin sacrebleu tok param. will include this test:

```
# tests/test_bleu_weights.py
refs = [["the cat is on the mat"]]
hyps = [["the cat is on mat"]]
# expected non-zero corpus BLEU > 0
```

marta: can you also add a debug flag to print intermediate counts when BLEU < threshold so we can triage quickly? :+1:

kevin: will do. also wondering if quantization changed segmentation (e.g., merging tokens) but since diff of hypotheses is identical, probably not.

jon: after the hotfix, run both sacrebleu versions in a canary job to validate outputs match. add a quick compare step in CI matrix.

kevin: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/1456 (WIP) — fixes integer division, pins sacrebleu tokenization arg, adds unit test and debug logging.

eval-bot: job=ci-eval-harness-build run=1456-checks status=queued

tara: once merged, can we backfill the nightly run that failed? we should re-score artifacts from build 8792 rather than re-run models.

ali: yes, add a rescore job that consumes hypotheses/*.json and produces new metrics. I'll add a flag to eval-bot to rescore-only.

kevin: quick note for postmortem: root cause = fragile metric code using int ops + coincidental sacrebleu upgrade. mitigation: stricter metric unit tests, version pinning in CI images, and add rescore path.

marta: sounds good. can we also add a small calibration test to catch huge deltas between float32 and quantized scoring? just a smoke threshold like BLEU change > 5 points -> fail CI and alert.

jon: agreed. include histogram logging of per-sentence BLEU diffs in console output for that smoke test.

kevin: ok i'll finish PR and request reviews from you all. thanks for quick help. :rocket:

ali: thanks — logging ticket for follow-up: #TICKET-2213 (eval-metrics hardening)

kevin: eval-bot: please rerun checks when PR pushed.

eval-bot: ack — will re-run on push.
